title: Add Probes to an Application
description: Deploy an nginx Pod with readiness, liveness, and startup probes and observe their effect.
problemStatement:
## 🎯 Goal
Configure a Pod with all three probes to understand their lifecycle.

### Steps
1. Create a Pod YAML `probes-demo.yaml` with:
   - container: nginx:1.25
   - startup probe: httpGet on `/` port 80, initialDelaySeconds 0, periodSeconds 5, failureThreshold 6 (30s total)
   - readiness probe: httpGet on `/` port 80, periodSeconds 5, failureThreshold 2
   - liveness probe: httpGet on `/health` port 80 (nginx doesn't have /health by default, so this will fail), periodSeconds 5, failureThreshold 3, initialDelaySeconds 0 (but remember startup probe gates it)
2. Apply the Pod.
3. Watch the Pod: `kubectl get pods -w`. The startup probe should succeed quickly (nginx serves /), so the Pod becomes Running and Ready.
4. After a while, the liveness probe will fail because `/health` returns 404. Wait until the container restarts (`kubectl get pods` will show RESTARTS).
5. Check logs or describe to see the restart event.
6. (Optional) Modify the probe to point to a valid path and update.
7. Delete the Pod.
hints: The startup probe will succeed because nginx returns 200 on /. So liveness will start after startup succeeds.
Liveness probe failing leads to container restart after failureThreshold consecutive failures.
Use `kubectl describe pod probes-demo` to see probe failures and restarts.
expectedOutput: The Pod initially starts; after liveness fails enough, it restarts.
solutionCode:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: probes-demo
spec:
  containers:
  - name: nginx
    image: nginx:1.25
    startupProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /
        port: 80
      periodSeconds: 5
      failureThreshold: 6
    readinessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /
        port: 80
      periodSeconds: 5
      failureThreshold: 2
    livenessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /health
        port: 80
      periodSeconds: 5
      failureThreshold: 3
